description: This topic teaches Form 1 learners how to write invitations and friendly letters, read and create timetables, hold dialogues, give clear directions, and recognise non-verbal communication cues for effective everyday and functional writing.

mcq.questionText: Which greeting begins a friendly letter to your uncle?
mcq.explanation: 'Dear Uncle,' is a warm, personal greeting suited to a family member rather than a stranger or a business contact. Exam Tip: friendly letters use warm greetings, while formal letters use distant ones such as 'Dear Sir/Madam'.

mcq.questionText: Which is the correct FIRST stage in the writing process?
mcq.explanation: Pre-writing is where ideas are planned and generated before any drafting begins. Exam Tip: remember the order pre-writing, then drafting, then revising, then editing.

mcq.questionText: An invitation card for a birthday party should typically include:

options.text: The date, time, venue and purpose of the event
A long essay about the host's life

mcq.explanation: An invitation must communicate the essential practical details a guest needs. Exam Tip: always check an invitation covers WHO, WHAT occasion, WHEN and WHERE.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly demonstrates giving directions?

options.text: The school is somewhere in town.
Turn left at the market, then go straight until you reach the school.
I don't know where the school is.

mcq.explanation: Step-by-step guidance with clear actions helps a listener actually find the place. Exam Tip: good directions combine clear action verbs with specific landmarks.

mcq.questionText: A dialogue is best described as:

options.text: A conversation between two or more people

mcq.explanation: A dialogue is an exchange of spoken words between two or more participants. Exam Tip: dialogues show back-and-forth exchange, often written with each speaker's name.

mcq.questionText: Which correctly expresses possession for a timetable exercise?

options.text: I have a timetable for this week.

mcq.explanation: 'Have' is the correct present tense form to use with the subject 'I'. Exam Tip: remember I/you/we/they take 'have', while he/she/it takes 'has'.

mcq.questionText: When writing a friendly letter to family, which closing is most appropriate?
mcq.explanation: A warm, personal closing matches the informal, affectionate tone of a family letter. Exam Tip: formal letters close with 'Yours faithfully/sincerely'; friendly letters use warmer closings.

mcq.questionText: A weekly timetable would most usefully include:

options.text: Days of the week and planned activities for each time slot

mcq.explanation: A timetable exists to organise time-based activities by day, so it must show days and their planned activities. Exam Tip: timetables are usually presented as a grid or table.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence demonstrates awareness of non-verbal cues (gestures, expressions, tone)?

options.text: She said nothing and made no gestures, giving away nothing.
She frowned and crossed her arms, showing she was upset even before speaking.

mcq.explanation: Frowning and crossed arms are physical, non-verbal cues that reveal emotion without any words being spoken. Exam Tip: non-verbal cues often carry meaning alongside, or instead of, spoken words.

mcq.questionText: Which opening would be appropriate for a short story?

options.text: Once upon a time, there lived a poor farmer in a small village.

mcq.explanation: 'Once upon a time' is a classic opening phrase used to begin traditional stories. Exam Tip: common story openers include 'Once upon a time...', 'Long ago...' and 'One day...'.

mcq.questionText: When speaking with an elder or higher-status person, which style is most appropriate?

options.text: Exactly the same casual slang as with friends

mcq.explanation: Communication norms require more polite and formal language when speaking to elders or people of higher status. Exam Tip: adjusting your formality to the listener's age or status is an important speaking skill.

mcq.questionText: In a friendly letter, the sender's address is typically written:

options.text: At the top, usually right-aligned, followed by the date
In the middle of the body

mcq.explanation: Standard letter layout places the sender's address at the top, followed by the date, before the greeting. Exam Tip: memorise the standard layout order: address and date, greeting, body, closing, signature.

mcq.questionText: Which expresses an ongoing activity happening right now?

options.text: She is cooking dinner right now.

mcq.explanation: 'Is cooking...right now' uses the present progressive tense, which describes an action in progress at this moment. Exam Tip: the present progressive (is/am/are + -ing) is the standard tense for a current activity.

mcq.questionText: A student wants to give directions to a classroom. Which is clearest?

options.text: Walk past the library, then turn right; the classroom is the second door on your left.
The classroom exists in the school building.

mcq.explanation: Specific, step-by-step directions using landmarks genuinely help a listener find the place. Exam Tip: vague directions fail the whole communicative purpose of giving directions.

mcq.questionText: Which best demonstrates expressing family relationships and occupations?

options.text: My father is a teacher and my mother is a nurse.
My father teacher, my mother nurse.

mcq.explanation: A complete, grammatically correct sentence clearly expresses both the relationship and the occupation of each family member. Exam Tip: always use full, grammatically complete sentences to communicate clearly.

fib.questionText: A friendly letter typically begins with a warm greeting such as '_____ Mother,' or '_____ Uncle,'.
fib.explanation: 'Dear' followed by the family member's name is the standard warm opening for a friendly letter. Exam Tip: friendly letters always begin with 'Dear' plus the person's name or title.

fib.questionText: The first stage of the writing process, planning before drafting, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Pre-writing is the planning stage where ideas are generated before the first draft is written. Exam Tip: pre-writing always comes first in the writing process.

fib.questionText: An invitation card should include date, time, _____ and purpose of the event.
fib.explanation: The venue tells guests exactly where the event will be held, which is essential information. Exam Tip: an invitation must always state WHO, WHAT, WHEN and WHERE.

fib.questionText: A conversation between two or more people, often written with each speaker's exact words, is a _____.
fib.explanation: A dialogue records the exact spoken exchange between two or more speakers. Exam Tip: dialogues are usually laid out with each speaker's name before their words.

fib.questionText: A friendly letter to family often closes with '_____ love,' before the signature.
fib.explanation: 'With love,' is a warm complimentary close commonly used in friendly letters to family. Exam Tip: warm closings like 'With love,' suit friendly letters, not formal ones.

fib.questionText: A weekly _____ organises planned activities by day and time.
fib.explanation: A timetable is a structured chart that shows activities arranged by day and time slot. Exam Tip: timetables are usually presented in a grid or table format.

fib.questionText: Facial expressions, gestures and tone of voice are examples of _____ communication cues.
fib.explanation: Facial expressions, gestures and tone all communicate meaning without using spoken or written words, so they are non-verbal cues. Exam Tip: non-verbal cues can support or even contradict spoken words.

fib.questionText: A classic story-opening phrase is '_____ upon a time'.
fib.explanation: 'Once upon a time' is the traditional fixed phrase used to open fairy tales and folk stories. Exam Tip: this exact phrase signals the start of a traditional narrative.

fib.questionText: When speaking with elders or higher-status people, it is appropriate to use more _____ language.
fib.explanation: Politeness and respect increase when speaking to elders or people of higher status. Exam Tip: match your level of formality to who you are speaking to.

fib.questionText: In a friendly letter, the sender's _____ and the date are usually written at the top.
fib.explanation: The sender's address is placed at the top of a friendly letter, with the date written just below it. Exam Tip: address and date always appear before the greeting in letter layout.

tf.questionText: Friendly letters typically use warm, personal greetings such as 'Dear Mother,'.
tf.explanation: A friendly letter is written to someone close, so it opens with a warm, personal greeting rather than a formal one.

tf.questionText: Pre-writing is the final stage of the writing process, done after editing.
tf.explanation: Pre-writing is actually the first stage, where ideas are planned before drafting, revising and editing take place.

tf.questionText: An invitation should include date, time, venue and purpose.
tf.explanation: These four details tell a guest exactly what the event is, and when and where it is happening.

tf.questionText: A dialogue involves only one person speaking with no interaction.
tf.explanation: A dialogue is an exchange between two or more speakers; a single speaker with no interaction is a monologue.

tf.questionText: Giving directions should include specific landmarks and action words like 'turn'/'go straight'.
tf.explanation: Clear directions rely on landmarks and action verbs so the listener can follow the route step by step.

tf.questionText: Non-verbal cues include only written words, with no gestures or expressions.
tf.explanation: Non-verbal cues are gestures, facial expressions and tone of voice, not written words.

tf.questionText: A weekly timetable typically organises activities by day and time.
tf.explanation: A timetable is a grid that arranges planned activities according to the day and time slot.

tf.questionText: When speaking with peers, the same formality is expected as with elders/leaders.
tf.explanation: Speaking with peers usually allows more casual language, while elders and leaders are addressed more formally.

tf.questionText: Traditional stories often begin with 'Once upon a time'.
tf.explanation: This fixed phrase is the classic opening used to signal the start of a traditional story.

tf.questionText: 'Yours faithfully' is most appropriate for writing to a close family member.
tf.explanation: 'Yours faithfully' is a formal closing for business or official letters, not for a warm family letter.

summary.correctAnswer: A short written notice inviting someone to an event, stating the date, time, venue and purpose.
summary.explanation: It focuses on essential practical details rather than long descriptions.

summary.correctAnswer: A conversation between two or more people, usually written with each speaker's exact words.
summary.explanation: Dialogues are often set out with the speaker's name before their words.

summary.correctAnswer: A chart or table that organises planned activities by day and time.
summary.explanation: Weekly timetables help plan study, work or school activities in an orderly way.

summary.correctAnswer: Signals such as facial expressions, gestures and tone of voice that communicate meaning without spoken words.
summary.explanation: They can support or even contradict what is being said out loud.

summary.correctAnswer: A personal letter written to family or friends using a warm greeting, informal tone and affectionate closing.
summary.explanation: It differs from a formal letter in tone, greeting and closing.

summary.correctAnswer: The greeting that opens a letter, such as 'Dear Uncle,' or 'Dear Sir/Madam,'.
summary.explanation: The choice of salutation depends on how well the writer knows the reader.

summary.correctAnswer: The polite phrase used to end a letter before the signature, such as 'With love,' or 'Yours faithfully,'.
summary.explanation: Warm closings suit friendly letters, while formal closings suit official letters.

summary.correctAnswer: The planning stage of writing in which ideas are generated and organised before drafting begins.
summary.explanation: It is always the first step in the writing process.

summary.correctAnswer: Explaining how to reach a place using clear action words and specific landmarks in the correct order.
summary.explanation: Good directions let a stranger follow the route without prior knowledge.

summary.correctAnswer: The level of politeness and formality used in language, adjusted according to who is being addressed.
summary.explanation: Speaking to an elder or leader calls for a more polite register than speaking to a close friend.

hoq.questionText: Draft the KEY elements a letter to an aunt inviting her to a graduation ceremony should include.

options.text: A warm greeting, event details (date/time/venue/purpose), a polite invitation phrase, and a warm closing, combining emotional warmth with practical information

hoq.explanation: A complete invitation letter must combine a warm family tone with all the practical details an aunt needs to attend. Exam Tip: functional writing is graded on both correct format/tone and completeness of information.

hoq.questionText: Which sample gives effective directions from the school gate to the library using landmarks and sequencing?

options.text: 'From the school gate, walk straight until the assembly hall. Then turn right and continue past the staff room. The library is the second building on your left.'

hoq.explanation: Effective directions combine action verbs, specific landmarks and sequence words so a listener can follow each step in order. Exam Tip: imagine a stranger following your exact words with no prior knowledge of the place.

hoq.questionText: Why does a dialogue between a student and teacher need different politeness than one between two close friends?

options.text: There is no real difference between the two situations

Speaking with a teacher, who has higher status, requires more polite language (e.g. 'Good morning, teacher. May I ask a question, please?'), while friends allow casual language (e.g. 'Hey, can I ask you something?')
Teachers and friends should always use slang
The formality expected is reversed from what is normal

hoq.explanation: The relationship and relative status between speakers shapes the appropriate level of politeness, which is a key 'register' awareness skill. Exam Tip: recognising WHO you are speaking to should directly shape HOW you speak.
